_provenance.note: SHA-256 prefixes of the code that produced this artefact. If these disagree with the working tree, the artefact predates a code change and must be regenerated. Check with `python -m provenance` from `common/`.

e1_occupancy.reading: Occupancy is the fraction of the L position columns a token actually fills. Everything below it is zeros. This is the waste the assignment describes, and it is real, but zeros cost dimensions and nothing else.
e1_occupancy.unit: token, as produced by the assignment-2 tokenizer

e2_characters_per_window.reading: A window of L bytes is a window of L characters only for scripts that cost one byte per character. For a 3-byte script the same architectural constant buys a third of the context. Graphemes are approximated, and the grapheme figure is the one that matters for a reader, since a Devanagari conjunct is written as several codepoints but read as one unit.

e3_by_lane_and_script.reading: The prose lanes (web, long_ctx, reasoning) are the fair English baseline. The code and math lanes are Latin script but not language, and they carry almost all of the pooled Latin collisions.

e3_collision_check.claim: distinct words sharing a first-L-byte prefix receive the identical embedding
